items.article_search_text: Keanu Reeves gets behind the wheel to chauffeur Max Verstappen, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri to the Las Vegas GP podium ceremony. The celebrations after the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix took an unexpected turn when Hollywood star Keanu Reeves stepped into the driver’s seat, giving the three podium finishers a limousine ride around the famous Strip. A video shared by Formula 1 showed Reeves behind the wheel of a limousine carrying race winner Max Verstappen and McLaren drivers Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. The trio were seen waving to fans as the vehicle made its way through the illuminated streets, with the spectacle providing a distinctly Las Vegas ending to an already dramatic night. Reeves’ appearance was more than a brief celebrity cameo. The actor took the top three on a post-race lap around the Las Vegas Strip Circuit and was also pictured driving them towards their post-race interviews. The unusual arrangement brought together the worlds of Hollywood and Formula 1, with the drivers enjoying a different kind of victory lap after climbing out of their cars. The 2026 race had offered plenty of its own drama. Verstappen started from pole position and held off repeated challenges to secure his third Las Vegas Grand Prix victory. The Red Bull driver crossed the line just 0.639 seconds ahead of Norris, while Piastri finished another 1.529 seconds behind in third. The match featured 35 changes of the lead, as Verstappen traded places with the Mercedes drivers before the team’s challenge faded in the closing stages. George Russell hit the barriers late in the race, while Kimi Antonelli slipped behind both McLarens, allowing Norris and Piastri to complete the podium. For Reeves, the appearance also reflected an interest in motorsport. The 62-year-old actor hosted and executive-produced the documentary series Brawn: The Impossible Formula 1 Story, which revisited Brawn GP’s remarkable 2009 championship-winning season. He has also taken part in competitive racing, making his professional debut in the Toyota GR Cup at Indianapolis in 2024. items.article_search_text: erstappen Wins Las Vegas Grand Prix as Norris, Piastri Take Podium Uncovering the Continent Through Its Own Lens Breaking news and current affairs from across Africa Latest news and updates from Somalia Breaking news and analysis from Kenya Current affairs and news from Ethiopia African business news, markets, and economic analysis Political news and governance across East Africa United States, November 22, 2026 — Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix for Red Bull on Saturday night, 21 November, beating McLaren's Lando Norris by 0.639 seconds in a race where the lead changed hands repeatedly. Oscar Piastri completed the podium for McLaren, 1.529 seconds behind the winner. Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes finished fourth, followed by Alpine's Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto, according to the official Formula 1 race report. Verstappen started from pole position after Antonelli, the fastest driver in qualifying, took a five-place grid penalty for a power unit change. George Russell of Mercedes pressed the Dutchman for much of the 50 laps, and the two traded the lead several times. Russell locked up on lap 48 and dropped to ninth, while Antonelli appeared to suffer a problem and slipped behind both McLarens. "It was just a crazy amount of fighting," Verstappen said, adding that the slipstream on the long straights made it almost impossible to pull clear. It was his third victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. A Safety Car was deployed mid-race after Sergio Perez of Cadillac collided with Haas driver Rafael Camara. Perez retired from the race. Red Bull's Isack Hadjar ran third after the restart but lost his front wing and fell back. He finished 14th on the road, and a 10-second post-race penalty moved him down to 15th. Ferrari had a difficult night. Lewis Hamilton took a 10-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage while fighting Norris, and later made contact with his team-mate Charles Leclerc. Leclerc received a 10-second penalty of his own. Hamilton finished seventh and Leclerc tenth, with Carlos Sainz eighth for Williams in his 250th Grand Prix. RaceFans' points table shows Antonelli on 402 points, Verstappen on 304 and Hamilton on 267 after 21 of 23 rounds. Antonelli's lead over Verstappen is 98 points (402 minus 304), more than the 50 points available in the final two races. The Qatar Grand Prix at the Lusail International Circuit on 27–29 November is the penultimate round of the season.

items.article_search_text: Oscar Piastri enjoyed a Las Vegas overtaking masterclass, with the Australian claiming an unexpected Formula 1 podium from the back Oscar Piastri enjoyed a Las Vegas overtaking masterclass, with the Australian claiming an unexpected F1 podium from the back of the grid. Motorsport Week is an independent, FIA accredited motorsport website delivering the latest Formula 1, Formula E, GP2, GP3, WEC, IndyCar, Nascar, Formula 3, WRC, WRX, DTM, IMSA and MotoGP news and results. Oscar Piastri enjoyed a Las Vegas overtaking masterclass, with the Australian claiming an unexpected Formula 1 podium from the back of the grid. In a difficult season for the McLaren driver, Piastri headed to the 'gambling capital of the world' to test his luck in F1. Ahead of the weekend, chances looked grim, as the Australian was hit with a ten-place grid penalty, in a season where the MCL40 has struggled for pace. But despite starting 17th in Vegas, Piastri capitalised on the chaos and close racing through the field, slowly moving his McLaren into the top spots, challenging his team-mate Lando Norris and the Mercedes duo in particular. Reflecting on the race, the 25-year-old highlighted that it was a strategic race for the ages. The Safety Car and Mercedes' mistakes, in particular, played into McLaren's hands for a double podium. "Yeah, it was crazy," Piastri concluded. "I think, as Lando kind of said, it was a lot about playing your cards at the right time." "I think from where I was, I think we were very quick in the corners, so then you could stay very close in the slipstream, which was good." "But yeah, the timing of the safety car was a bit unfortunate because we had to do a double stack in the pit stop, so I kind of went back again and had to fight my way back." Piastri understood from very early in the race that the race was going to be chaotic. Thus, opening many opportunities for himself to get to the front of the pack. Crucially, the McLaren driver played his cards right and was very happy with an unexpected second-place finish. "But no, from that far back, I think I kind of worked out pretty early on that it was going to be a pretty chaotic race. And that there were going to be a lot of opportunities throughout the whole thing. Even from where we were." "So, I'm very happy that we made the right decisions at the right time and were able to end up on the podium." https://twitter.com/F1/status/2124408791643082897?a=T4luaNAdsRLDoYshzSk&s=20 Oscar Piastri explains MCL40 handling issues despite Las Vegas podium Whilst the Australian secured just his third podium of the season, it hasn't eradicated the issues he has faced with this year's challenger. Throughout the season, Piastri has struggled to extract the same pace as his team-mate Norris, ulimately having a more difficult time adjusting to the sweeping 2026 regulations. When asked if this was the most comfortable he's been all season, Piastri explained the rollercoaster his season has been with the MCL40. "No, I don't think so," he said. "The last few races have been up and down. "I think the ups have been back at the level that they should be. And the downs obviously are not where they should be." However, there was still a higher level of comfort at times throughout the weekend than what Piastri has grown accustomed to in previous races. Ultimately, the McLaren driver pointed to the team's development for next season, where they will hopefully return to form. "But yeah, I was a bit more comfortable this weekend, not necessarily all the time. But again, I think we're still working on it." "Some things hopefully will be better next year. We'll see. Yeah, I don't think today's result was necessarily because I was any more comfortable." READ MORE – Lando Norris explains key McLaren issue en route to Las Vegas podium

Photograph: Jeenah Moon/ReutersKey PointsLando Norris finished second and Oscar Piastri finished third at the Las Vegas Grand Prix.The McLaren duo were disqualified from last years Las Vegas GP for excessive skid plank wear.Piastri joked about waiting for final technical checks before celebrating to avoid a repeat of last years disqualification.Norris stated that last years disqualification was a freak thing and not a motivation for this years performance.McLaren is currently fourth in the constructors championship, nine points behind Red Bull. McLarens Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri said they were pleased to put last years double disqualification at the Las Vegas Grand Prix behind them after finishing second and third on Saturday.Norris had started from pole position and finished second in Las Vegas last year, while Piastri crossed the line fourth, but both were later disqualified for excessive skid plank wear.A Redemption Race in VegasOn Saturday, Norris and Piastri followed home race winner Max Verstappen, with Piastri joking that he would save his celebrations until the final technical checks were complete. I dont know if were past scrutineering yet. Im hoping we have, the Australian told reporters.No, its good. And yeah, in the context of this years championship its exactly what we needed. So Im very happy about that. But yeah, Im not going to solidify my comments until we have actually passed scrutineering.Championship Standings and OutlookMcLaren won the constructors championship last year but are fourth this season, nine points behind Red Bull in third. items.article_search_text: Oscar Piastri says McLaren's double podium in Las Vegas delivered a crucial boost as the team closed to nine points behind Red Bull. McLaren strengthened its challenge for the Formula 1 Constructors' Championship with a double podium at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, where Oscar Piastri recovered from 17th on the grid to finish third. The Australian described the result as an important boost for the team after an eventful 50-lap race on the Las Vegas street circuit.According to Formula 1, Piastri started 17th after receiving a 10-place grid penalty for changing power unit components ahead of the weekend. He worked his way through the field before challenging teammate Lando Norris for the final podium position.Both McLaren drivers overtook Kimi Antonelli's Mercedes on the final lap, securing the team's second double podium of the season. The result also reduced McLaren's deficit to Red Bull to nine points in the Constructors' Championship, despite Max Verstappen taking the race victory.Piastri highlighted the team's recovery during the race and the importance of collecting points in the championship battle."It was a lot of fun. It was pretty entertaining, that’s for sure. It was just a crazy race," said Piastri.The Australian explained that his progress during the opening laps was interrupted by the timing of the Safety Car. He also lost ground after stopping behind Norris during the pit sequence before fighting his way back toward the front."I made really good progress in the first few laps, and then a bit unfortunate with the timing of the Safety Car so I kind of dropped back halfway again [after stacking behind Norris in the pits]. Made our way towards the front, which was great, and I think also for the team this was exactly the kind of result we needed for the Constructors’ Championship. Very happy with the day’s work."The Las Vegas result marked Piastri's third podium of the season. His previous appearance on the podium came at the Miami Grand Prix in May, while Norris had secured three victories during the campaign.Despite welcoming his latest podium, Piastri remained cautious about what the performance meant for his overall pace. He noted that the unusual characteristics of the Las Vegas race made it difficult to draw firm conclusions about McLaren's progress."It’s hard to say. Definitely I think the pace in general was pretty strong so I was happy with things, but that was such a particular race," said Piastri.He also pointed to the differences expected at the upcoming events, emphasizing that the team would need to maintain its performance across different racing conditions."The next two weeks are not going to look like that, that’s for sure. I think the pace was good so we’ll just try and keep it rolling for the next two weeks."

items.article_search_text: Oscar Piastri questions McLaren's straight-line speed deficit against other Mercedes-powered cars after a disappointing Las Vegas qualifying session. McLaren's straight-line speed disadvantage has raised fresh concerns after Oscar Piastri questioned why the team trails other Mercedes-powered competitors at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The Australian driver highlighted an unexpected performance gap during qualifying, despite McLaren anticipating difficulties at the high-speed circuit.Piastri secured seventh place in final qualifying, while teammate Lando Norris finished fifth. However, Piastri faces a 10-place grid penalty for exceeding Formula 1's seasonal allowance of four internal combustion engines after installing his fifth unit.According to Motorsport.com, Piastri also received an upgraded turbocharger specification developed by Mercedes through the FIA's Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) framework.Piastri acknowledged that his qualifying performance had been inconsistent, particularly during the decisive third session."After Q2, I was pretty happy with how it went," Piastri said.He explained that securing an effective slipstream was particularly important at the Las Vegas circuit, where small differences in energy deployment could significantly affect straight-line performance."And then Q3 was just a bit messy for a few reasons. Trying to get the right slipstream is… you might as well not even go out if you don't get that right," Piastri said.He also identified differences in how cars manage energy before the opening corner as another factor affecting their speed later in the lap."Even opening the lap here, I think there's a bit of a difference between cars, how much energy they use to turn one and if that's half a second, that can be the difference of three or four tenths down the straight later in the lap," Piastri said.McLaren's performance difficulties are linked partly to aerodynamic limitations and its technical decisions. The team selected lower gear ratios and the shortest permissible wheelbase to reduce weight, choices that have restricted some opportunities to improve aerodynamic performance.The team also introduced a revised floor for Las Vegas, but only one specification was ready in time for the event. Norris received the updated component, although his Q3 performance was affected when a plastic bag became trapped around one of its floor fences.Piastri said the difference between McLaren and other Mercedes-powered cars was particularly difficult to explain."It's difficult to know and it caught us by surprise, to be honest. I don't think we expected it to be such a big problem. At Monza we were okay and the strange part for us is it's mostly compared with the other Mercedes-powered cars," Piastri said.He suggested that differences in aerodynamic downforce configurations could be contributing to the performance gap, although he acknowledged that the team still needed to understand the underlying problem."So, maybe a lot of people took downforce off and we didn't take enough off, but it seems like a pretty massive step that we were missing in practice. I don't know if it's still the same now, but definitely we seem, for one reason or another, to be pretty slow on the straights," Piastri said.Telemetry data from the fastest Q3 laps showed Piastri losing as much as 10 kilometers per hour to Alpine drivers Franco Colapinto and Pierre Gasly on the main straight along the Las Vegas Strip. Piastri compensated by braking later and maintaining throttle deeper into several corners.McLaren team principal Andrea Stella acknowledged that the circuit exposed weaknesses in the car's overall performance, particularly when aerodynamic drag, engine characteristics and slipstream effects combined."Definitely, we had some concern in terms of how suitable the demand of this circuit will be for our car," Stella said.Stella explained that the team's existing gear ratios and aerodynamic characteristics affected its ability to maximize performance at high speeds. He emphasized that McLaren needed to evaluate several interacting factors rather than focusing exclusively on maximum speed."For reasons that we have talked about before, developing speed at very high speed. Because this is not only the top speed, it is also the top speed that combines with the towing that everyone tries to see. So, you go in operating regimes of the engine that with our [gear] ratios are not ideal.We know that the drag from an aerodynamic point of view is not a point of strength. But we discussed in the debrief that we need to look holistically at all the conditions that influence the top speed," Stella said.Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli demonstrated the potential advantage of slipstreaming by recording the fastest time while running closely behind Racing Bulls driver Arvid Lindblad. The Las Vegas circuit's slippery slow corners and cold November conditions made the aerodynamic effects of following another car less damaging to cornering performance.

items.article_search_text: Oscar Piastri defended McLaren's racing approach after finishing third in Las Vegas, insisting he and Lando Norris understood how to compete safely. McLaren secured a valuable double podium at the Las Vegas Grand Prix after Oscar Piastri recovered from 17th on the grid to finish third behind Max Verstappen and Lando Norris. The Australian driver also dismissed suggestions that he and Norris needed additional instructions from the team while competing against each other during the closing stages of the race.According to Motorsport.com, Piastri started with a 10-place grid penalty following an engine change. His third-place finish marked his first podium since the Miami Grand Prix in May, while Norris secured second behind race winner Verstappen.The two McLaren drivers engaged in a late-race battle, with Norris eventually overtaking his teammate. The team's management had reminded both drivers to exercise caution, but Piastri maintained that they already understood their responsibilities on track.Responding to questions from Sky Sports about the team's instructions, Piastri defended their racing judgment."Yeah, we know what we're doing. We don't need to be told," said Piastri.He emphasized that maximizing the team's championship points remained their priority despite the close competition. Both drivers managed the situation without allowing their fight to compromise McLaren's result."For the team, that was a great result. We obviously got a little bit close at some points, but we were both very clear with what the goal was, which was to score as many points for the team as possible. So we definitely didn't race too hard. We raced each other very smart," Piastri said.Piastri also described the Las Vegas race as "bizarre" because of the unusual effects of aerodynamic slipstreaming, which made it difficult for drivers to establish a comfortable gap. He said McLaren generally had competitive pace but lacked some speed on the straights while performing better through corners."Obviously a massive pack, the slipstream being so important. Our pace generally was pretty good. We're obviously lacking a bit on the straights, but we're making up for it in the corners.It was just a bit odd in terms of the overtaking and where you would overtake. It wasn't normal. There was a bit of strategy involved with the buttons used, and where to use your energy, where to save it and stuff like that," Piastri said.Earlier in the Las Vegas weekend, both McLaren drivers had faced challenging weather conditions during Friday practice. According to GrandPrix.com, Piastri finished fifth in FP2 with a time of 1:48.453, while Norris placed seventh in 1:48.837.Piastri explained that skipping FP1 was a deliberate decision because heavy rain limited the value of running. FP2 provided an opportunity to gather information about the new internal combustion engine and turbocharger following his engine-related grid penalty."Overall, a positive session in FP2 after we chose not to run in FP1. With the rain in FP1, it didn't make much sense to go out as we weren't going to learn much, the conditions were bad, and we don't anticipate the rest of the weekend being the same. It was useful to get running in FP2 with the new Internal Combustion Engine and turbo so that we could learn as much as we could.It was an interesting and challenging session, with some good learnings on tyre warm-up. The initial few laps on the Inters were tricky but the car felt much more manageable as the conditions improved towards the end of the session, as a drier line started to appear. Looking ahead to tomorrow, while I have a 10-place grid penalty, it doesn't change our approach to the weekend.We will do what we can to maximise everything ahead of Qualifying and get ourselves up as high up as we can," Piastri said.Norris also highlighted the difficulties created by the wet surface and low temperatures. He said the team needed additional preparation before qualifying, particularly to evaluate new components and understand the car's behavior in dry conditions."It's good to be back on track here in Las Vegas, it's always an interesting place to drive an F1 car. This is a very low-grip, low-temperature circuit, and that's only been made more so by the rain today. In FP1, the level of rain meant there wasn't much value in going out, particularly when we expect it to be dry the rest of the weekend, but it was good to get some laps in during FP2, even if the conditions were still damp.We've got some important work to do tomorrow, particularly on testing some new bits and getting ready for Quali in dry conditions, so FP3 will be important. We'll do the best we can with the data we've gathered today and make sure we're ready to go tomorrow afternoon," Norris said.McLaren Senior Director of Racing Randy Singh explained that the weather also affected the team's technical development program. The engineers decided against installing a new floor because wet conditions and sensor limitations prevented them from collecting sufficiently reliable data."The conditions made it difficult to evaluate the car properly. In the wet, we had to tape up some of the sensors, which meant we could not always get the evidence we wanted, so we decided not to fit the new floor because of the risk and because we did not think we would learn much from it in these conditions. We hope to run it tomorrow and assess it more effectively.The rain and standing water made the track challenging, particularly with the walls so close, although the tyres held up well and we were able to do some useful work on the Intermediates as the rain eased. With both sessions wet, there is a lot to get through tomorrow, including preparation for Qualifying, and the programme will be compressed. It is clearly impossible to draw conclusions about our pace or likely positions: as usual, we can expect that the top four teams will be very close to each other, and the limited running of today makes it even more difficult to predict what there will be on the starting grid," Singh said.In the championship standings, Norris occupies fifth place with 264 points, level with George Russell in fourth according to Motorsport.com. Piastri sits seventh with 167 points, leaving McLaren with two drivers positioned inside the top seven as the season approaches its final two rounds.Mercedes also reported mixed findings from the rain-affected practice sessions. Russell topped FP2 with 1:47.272, although the team acknowledged that his fastest lap came when the circuit was at its driest. Kimi Antonelli finished eighth with 1:49.043."It's always nice to finish top of the times, but we know that doesn't tell the full story today. The conditions were changing throughout, and we got our lap in when the track was at its driest, while others looked very quick too. We weren't as competitive in the wet as we were last weekend, so there are a few things for us to understand overnight.Tomorrow will be busy if it stays dry and we'll want to maximise the running ahead of qualifying, particularly to learn about the tyres and any potential graining in these cold conditions. I'm feeling good at the moment though. We've been on the front row at the last two races, the performances have been strong, and this is a circuit I really enjoy.Hopefully we can build on that and have another good weekend," Russell said.Antonelli described the limited track time as an obstacle to establishing a consistent driving rhythm. He also identified intermediate-tyre performance as an area requiring further investigation."It was a strange day with the weather meaning we didn't get any real running in FP1 and no real representative running in FP2. It wasn't the easiest day therefore to build a rhythm. We still managed to learn a few things though and we have some things to look through overnight.We weren't as competitive as we would have liked on the Intermediate tyre so that will be useful to explore, even if it isn't learning that we will need for the rest of the weekend here in Las Vegas. Tomorrow should be a very different day if it stays dry, and FP3 will therefore be important. We'll need to maximise the running, get comfortable with the car in those conditions and understand the tyres, particularly with the limited information everyone has from today.I'm feeling positive though. The car has been performing well recently and hopefully we can have a productive final practice and put ourselves in a good position for qualifying," Antonelli said.

Oscar Piastri reiterated his displeasure with McLaren telling him to “be careful” following his podium finish at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Sunday afternoon’s race AEDT was arguably the Australian’s finest performance of the season as his third-place finish behind winner Max Verstappen and teammate Lando Norris was his first podium since Miami in early May. But one moment grabbed the attention of the F1 world more than Piastri’s stunning surge from starting 17th on the grid. In the latter stages of the race, Piastri had made it to fifth and set up a showdown with Norris and Mercedes pair Kimi Antonelli and George Russell to join Verstappen in spraying champagne post-race. In an uncommon display for frustration, he snapped at his race engineer Tom Stallard as he pushed to make up more ground but was handed down instructions to be mindful of Norris. “Stop telling me to f***ing be careful,” Piastri said over the team radio. Engineer: "You're doing a great race, but be careful around your teammate." Piastri: "Stop telling me to be ***** careful." — formularacers (@formularacers_) November 22, 2026 Piastri and Norris came wheel-to-wheel earlier in the race and have a history of unnecessary incidents, most notably in the Singapore sprint earlier this season. But Sky Sports’ Anthony Davidson pointed out on commentary that Piastri had every right to be frustrated with those orders that put McLaren’s infamous papaya rules in the spotlight yet again. “I kind of understand why Oscar is a little bit annoyed with that one, because when was the last time Oscar collided with his teammate? Usually it’s the other way around,” Davidson said on commentary. Asked about his comments over the team radio in his post-race press conference, Piastri was not in a mood to apologise. “Yeah, I mean, we know what we’re doing. We don’t need to be told,” he said with a grin. “So, yeah, I think for the team that was a great result. We got a little bit closer at some points, but we were both clear on what the goal was and that was to score as many points for the team as possible. “So, yeah, we definitely didn’t race each other too hard. We raced smart and made sure that we both stayed on the track.” Piastri had a point as other teams did not stay on track at the iconic Vegas Strip circuit. Russell ran into the wall on the penultimate lap when attempting to get past Antonelli. While Ferrari duo Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc derailed their race by making contact. STARTS P17 ➡️ FINISHES P3 An amazing drive from @OscarPiastri 💪 #F1 #LasVegasGP https://t.co/r3xa81axua — Formula 1 (@F1) November 22, 2026 Jacques Villeneuve, the 1997 world champion, said it was “great” to see Piastri showing a bit more of an edge, but agreed that the McLarens got the balance right. “That was a little bit surprising because you never hear any emotion or comments, that was great,” he said on Sky Sports. “Both drivers drove hard. Their race craft seemed good today – it’s not always been the case, look at last year, there’s been issues. “They also managed to optimise the situation because they didn’t have a car to be on the podium. “They waited for a few little mistakes and they pounced.” While Sky Sports analyst Jamie Chadwick added: “That’s not what I ever heard on the Ferrari radio. “Just constantly hearing be careful, be careful. Yes, it’s annoying if you’re Oscar, but at least it’s reminding the drivers.” When it came to the actual result, Piastri was understandably in a jovial mood. It was just his third podium of what has been a testing season but, on a weekend where McLaren deployed a new engine on the Australian’s car, it was a step in the right direction heading towards 2027. “I don’t know,” Piastri replied with a laugh when asked how he was able to achieve that result. “It was a bizarre race. Obviously, a massive pack with slip stream so important. I think our pace generally was pretty good. We’re obviously lacking a bit on the straights, but I think we’re making up for it on the corners. “And yeah, it was just a bit odd in terms of the overtaking and where you would overtake. It wasn’t normal - the only way I could put it. “There was a bit of strategy involved with the buttons used and when to use your energy, and when to save it. “I think we did a pretty good job of that.” In his interview with the television broadcasters following being escorted to the podium by Hollywood icon Keanu Reeves, Piastri also shed light on the craziness of the race that Verstappen and McLaren chief Zak Brown said could be the best F1 race of all-time. Quick word on Oscar Piastri Phenomenal drive to go from P17 to P3 when he also got screwed over in the pits under the SC Tough season this year but this result was excellent 👏 — Matt Gallagher (@MattP1Gallagher) November 22, 2026 Could’ve done with Keanu a few years ago when I was trying to get all 4 kids to Saturday morning sport at the same time 🙄 — Nicole Piastri (@NicolePiastri) November 22, 2026 "They say Las Vegas is the entertainment capital of the world and that was pretty entreating to be a part of,” Piastri said. "An amazing race. Starting from the back I didn't know how it would go and we could make progress pretty quick and I worked out pretty early on it was staying as one massive pack. "The double stack at the pit stop was a bit of a shame but it didn't really matter at the end. Everyone was in such a big pack. It was just bizarre to be a part of! "It was pretty random. You would pass someone on one straight super easy, then the next you would struggle then with someone else you had different strengths and weaknesses. "Every time you caught the back of the train you thought you would win the race by 10 seconds but then you would get ahead and realised the slipstream was doing a lot of help. "A crazy race to be a part of but very happy to end it on the podium." “Stop telling me to F****** be careful!”

Oscar Piastri has broken his silence over his decision to split from long-time Formula 1 manager Mark Webber ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix. According to Formula 1 , Piastri has explained why he and his management team, led by Mark and Ann Webber, mutually agreed to part ways, with the Australian believing the time was right for a new chapter in his career. The decision was announced following the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, bringing an end to a partnership that began in 2019 and helped Piastri secure his Formula 1 debut with McLaren in 2023. Speaking to the media in Las Vegas, Piastri reflected on the contribution the Webbers had made to his career, explaining that both parties had reached a point where pursuing separate paths felt like the right decision. He said, “We were just getting to a stage in our collaboration where it was better for us to go on our separate paths. Mark and Ann contributed so much to my career, both in placing me where I am today and the management of everything behind the scenes that nobody ever really sees. It felt like the time was right for something new.” “Mark played a massive part in my career, both Mark and Ann, at the end of my junior career, setting me up in Formula 1 and guiding me through those first few years. The impact they've had on my career has been enormous, and I think now it feels like the right time for us both to go on our separate adventures," Piastri added. The Webbers had already reduced their trackside involvement during the 2026 season, with Piastri's former PREMA race engineer Pedro Matos and mental coach Emma Murray taking on greater roles within his close team. "I think having the structure around you is an important thing, and it has looked a bit different this year already and will look a bit different again in the future, probably. In qualifying, drivers have found that if they increase their speed through a corner the power unit may deliver less energy on the following straight. Brown says grappling with this unusual feature of F1’s rules has proved a challenge for Piastri as well as other drivers this year. “I think we’ve seen the driver rosters get mixed up a bit this year,” he said. “Some have adapted quicker than others. These cars definitely take a different technique to drive. “I remember in the first race in Australia talking about [drivers needing to] slow down to speed up. Historically it’s always been about putting your foot down as quickly as possible, keeping it down as long as possible, braking as late as possible. These cars require a different driving technique.” Piastri has always been strong in very quick corners, said Brown, and McLaren had to tell him to slow down in them this year. “When you look at Oscar, he’s quite brave through the high-speed corners, which is a real strength of his,” said Brown. “Now you’ll hear us on the radio sometimes compromising some of those corners.” Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free Piastri led the championship for the majority of last season and was still in contention to win the world championship at the final round. items.article_search_text: New Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli will serve a five-place grid penalty for the Las Vegas Grand Prix; watch the Las Vegas GP on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 4am on Saturday and the race at 4am on Sunday Kimi Antonelli has received a five-place grid penalty for the Las Vegas Grand Prix after further exceeding his engine allocation for the season. New Formula 1 world champion Antonelli took his sixth internal combustion engine (ICE) of the season during Thursday's opening practice sessions in Las Vegas, breaching the limit of four across the year for the second time. Given the penalty for a second breach is five rather than 10 grid places, the Mercedes driver will start no higher than sixth in the race, which begins on Sunday morning at 4am UK time (build-up from 2.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 . Latest Sky Sports deals or stream F1 with no contract 📺 Antonelli started from the back of the grid at the Italian Grand Prix for exceeding the limit on several power unit elements, including his ICE, but remarkably won his home race in Monza. Mercedes have also fitted Antonelli with an upgraded turbocharger that they have brought to the event, but the Italian is not incurring a penalty for that as it is within his allowance of four for the season. In June, Mercedes were granted one chance to upgrade their power unit this season after being found to be between two and four per cent behind the best-performing internal combustion engine - which was unexpectedly judged to be Red Bull's - by the FIA in the year's first ADUO (Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities) assessment window. That ADUO upgrade, which Mercedes have focused on their power unit's turbo, is being used by seven of the eight Mercedes-powered cars on the grid, with Antonelli's team-mate George Russell the exception. Russell has already used five turbos, one more than is permitted, due to unreliability earlier in the year, and a sixth would trigger a further five-place grid penalty. The Briton, who dropped five places on the Sao Paulo Grand Prix grid due to an engine change, is in a five-way battle to finish runner-up to Antonelli in the standings with three races to go. Who else has grid penalties for the Las Vegas GP? McLaren's Oscar Piastri will serve a 10-place grid penalty as he has exceeded his ICE limit for the first time this season. Williams' Carlos Sainz also has a 10-place grid penalty for exceeding the turbocharger limit, and Aston Martin's Lance Stroll has the same penalty for a new energy store and control electronics. Oliver Bearman, who says he is "disappointed" to not have a Haas contract signed for 2027 , has changed several power unit elements and will start at the back of the grid. The long straights in Las Vegas means overtaking is relatively easy, so, in theory, it is a good track to take a grid penalty. Russell topped a rain-affected second practice on Thursday night in Las Vegas after the weather had prevented any lap times from being set in the opening session. The opening day of track action provided few clues of how the remainder of the weekend is likely to play out, with both qualifying and the race expected to take place in dry conditions. items.article_search_text: There's still plenty to play for in the final three rounds of the season, with the fight for second in the standings wide open. Read more at foxsports.com.au. The high-profile Las Vegas Grand Prix fires the starting gun on three races in three weeks to close the 2026 season with plenty still to play for. The finish line is in sight for Formula 1 in 2026. After 20 rounds of racing, just three grands prix remain, beginning with this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix. Formula 1 first conquered the Las Vegas Strip, shutting the neon-lit road for racing, three years ago in a highly hyped sporting coup. Watch the final 3 qualifying sessions in the 2026 F1® season Live and Free with Kayo Freebies. Watch FORMULA 1 HEINEKEN LAS VEGAS GRAND PRIX 2026 qualifying session on Saturday 21st November > Though the race has to some extent become part of the furniture after three grands prix, it remains among the highest profile events on the calendar for the sheer audacity of its location. Fortunately the track and the chilly night-time desert climate have a history of producing reliably good racing. Though the headline championship results are already settled, the final triple-header of the year — and unhinged combination of races that will see the sport fly more than 13,000 km to Qatar immediately after the chequered flag — has plenty still at stake. PIT TALK PODCAST: We look ahead to the beginning of the end of the Formula 1 season with this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix in one of the sport’s all-time great time zones, and it’s match point for Marc Márquez at this weekend’s MotoGP Portuguese Grand Prix. | Listen to Pit Talk below. CAN MERCEDES GET RUSSELL TO SECOND PLACE? Mercedes has won the constructors championship, and with Andrea Kimi Antonelli it’s won the drivers title too. But this glittering season isn’t complete with three rounds remaining. Mercedes wants a one-two championship finish. That means sneaking George Russell into second place. “Our targets are clear: helping George finish as high as possible in the drivers’ championship, ending the year with momentum, and continuing to unlock more performance from the car,” Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said. But while Antonelli has taken the title at a canter, Russell has lagged behind. He dropped to third several times during the European leg of the season and plummeted to fourth after the Mexico City Grand Prix. He’s now third but 17 points behind Max Verstappen for second. He’s also only one point clear or Lewis Hamilton in fourth. Drivers championship, battle for second Max Verstappen: 279 points George Russell: -17 points Lewis Hamilton: -18 points Charles Leclerc: -30 points Lando Norris: -33 points It’s far from an insurmountable gap, but Verstappen is in obviously better form. The Dutchman is on an eight-round podium streak and has won three of the last five grands prix. Russel’s last podium was his victory in Azerbaijan in September. It’s raised the prospect of Mercedes giving him a leg-up, perhaps even with a team orders advantage. “It could be a possibility that we’re giving it all the force,” Wolff hinted in Brazil. It would be a bizarre situation, the new champion giving up results to help who was his chief title rival to second place. Even just the prospect of team orders to secure a minor place on the title table is novel. Of course Mercedes hasn’t said that team orders will be used, and it’s hard to believe the team would lack self-awareness to such a degree that Antonelli might be asked to give up a victory or a podium to help Russell. Russell surely wouldn’t want a result handed to him like that anyway. For the let-down Englishman, it’s more important that he finish the season in good form than with a higher championship position. “For me what’s more important is just to have some strong weekends,” he said. “That doesn’t necessarily just mean the result; it just means from FP1 through the weekend showing good performances. “This season has been so up and down even during the weekend — even my strong weekends, other than Baku, sometimes it hasn’t been every lap of the weekend. “Of course I’d love to finish as high as possible, but that’s the most important thing.” The importance of finishing second, however, has prompted Russell not to use Mercedes’s upgraded turbocharger, which is making its debut this weekend, as using the new part would incur a grid penalty. Antonelli and multiple other Mercedes drivers will use the better turbo, though the team itself says the expected benefit is only minor. WHAT CAN PENALISED PIASTRI ACHIEVE? McLaren is bringing an upgraded car to this weekend, and Oscar Piastri will have to wield it to its maximum if he’s to get a big result. Piastri will start with one hand tied behind his back with a grid penalty for taking a new internal combustion engine, sending him 10 places down the order. He’ll also get the benefit of Mercedes’s new turbocharger, though this will come without penalty for him. With an average qualifying result of 6.4 this season, the Australian is likely to start around 16th on the grid. What he can achieve from well outside the points remains to be assessed through the practice sessions. “Just trying to maximise what we can do; we don’t know exactly where we’re going to sit with things,” he said. “Hopefully the new engine is going to help out a little bit — there are obviously going to be some spots to make up. “We’ll learn as much as we can about the race through practice — also I think we learned a lot in Monza about what qualifying could look like and the slipstreams and tows that people are going to want. “It’s going to be a pretty interesting qualifying session as well as race.” MORE FORMULA 1 ‘DOWN TO THE WIRE’: McLaren targets $15m payday… and Piastri’s form will be crucial PIT TALK: F1's newest team makes call on final 2027 seat; legend set for rally switch VEGAS RETROSPECTIVE: A catastrophic blunder turned Vegas into a 'horror movie'. McLaren is still paying the price What we do know ahead of time, though, is that Las Vegas is historically a weak McLaren circuit, and it isn’t expected to suit the car any better this weekend. The McLaren car doesn’t like short, slow corners or long straights, but that’s pretty much all there is in Las Vegas. The track has a similar profile to Azerbaijan, where the car was 0.8s off the pace. Paradoxically, though, Baku was actually one of Piastri’s stronger weekends, having been on for a podium before the race unravelled late. It was the first in a run of races in which Piastri has felt himself getting more comfortable in the car. “I think in general it’s been looking a bit better recently,” he said. “Austin and Mexico maybe not quite so much, but I felt like through Malaysia, Singapore, Baku and then Brazil as well the results maybe weren’t always what they could’ve been on those weekends, but the feeling in the car was definitely an improvement. “[In Brazil] qualifying was a shame because the pace I had on Sunday was the strongest it’s been for a while. “That’s the big positive. It’s just about trying to convert that potential now into results.” It's important to McLaren that Piastri finds form as it seeks to overhaul Red Bull Racing for third in the constructors championship, but good form might be enoguh for only minor points this weekend. HAMILTON DENIES FERRARI TRUST PROBLEMS There’s no denying Lewis Hamilton has had a strong season — a far, far stronger season than he had last year — but his more competitive campaign has uncovered deep cracks in Ferrari as a title-challenging prospect. The power unit isn’t up to scratch, but that’s part of the game to some extent. The executional errors have been more painful but at least explainable in the context of this being a deeply inexperienced Ferrari team — the Scuderia hasn’t won a championship in almost two decades. But the appearance of conflict and tension between Hamilton and Charles Leclerc has been harder to handle. More problematic still is what looks like trust issue between Hamilton and his team. In Singapore and in Brazil — twice in the last four grands prix — Hamilton disobeyed orders to pit for fresh tyres, appearing to believe he could better dictate strategy from the cockpit. On both occasions it backfired. In Singapore he tumbled out of podium contention, and in Brazil he spun off the track in the wet. Hamilton wouldn’t be the first driver to lack faith in Ferrari’s strategy calls, but the seven-time champion didn’t so much argue as he did unilaterally ignore the calls to the detriment of both the team and to his standing in the drivers championship. Speaking Las Vegas, Hamilton denied he and Ferrari had trust issues but admitted more work had to be done to hone the team collectively. "We're constantly working on our communication," he said, per the BBC. "It's been a lot better this year. Carlo [Santi, Hamilton’s new race engineer] has done an amazing job, and those particular two times [in Singapore and Brazil], particularly the last time, was just I didn't have the information I needed. I got the call right at the last minute. "We'll just continue to work on the processes. We're super united in what's working, in the right direction." In the context of Mercedes having been destined to control both championships this season, Ferrari’s 2026 can be written off as a crucial learning year — learning not only about the new rules but also about how to handle a competitive line-up with Hamilton alongside Charles Leclerc. But the team has only three races remaining to iron out these problems before the 2027 acid test begins. STROLL HOMES IN ON UNWANTED RECORD Lance Stroll is on the cusp of one of Formula 1’s most unwanted records: most DNFs in a single season. Because this is motorsport, the record is more complicated than you might think. Andrea de Cesaris holds the record for most failures to finish in a season. In the 1987 season, he failed to finish every single one of the 16 rounds. However, though he didn’t see the chequered flag at any race, he was classified twice for having completed 90 per cent of the race distance before running into problems. One of those two classifications was the Belgian Grand Prix, where he remarkably finished third in a race that saw a sensational 24 of 26 drivers fail to make the finish. The alternative record is most non-classifications — what we would usually describe as a DNF (did not finish). De Cesaris also holds the record for most non-classifications in a season with the 14 DNFs he accrued in 1987. Where does Stroll stand against these benchmarks? The Canadian has 13 DNFs for the season. However, he was also not classified at the Australian Grand Prix for not having completed 90 per cent of the race despite seeing the chequered flag — he spent 15 laps in his garage due to problems with his car and engine, too many to be included in the results. Therefore he’s already equalled De Cesaris’s 14-race record for non-classifications. One more would see him hold the record outright. The break the record for non-finishes, however, he would have to retire from all of the remaining three grands prix this season. Of course the significantly longer season has ‘helped’ his cause here. De Cesaris will almost certainly always hold both records on a percentage basis. But modern F1 is also far more reliable than in the days of De Cesaris’s famously problem-prone career, which saw him retire from a staggering 146 races in his 208-start career — a non-finishing rate of 70.2 per cent. The sheer number of retirements, therefore, is still impressive. “I heard about it,” Stroll said of the record. “We’ve had a lot of issues out there, a lot of engine problems. “It’s been a tough year for the whole team. That being said, it might not be such a happy or chirpy outing for the massively talented youngster from the Kangaroo land as Las Vegas might just be a peculiar challenge for Oscar Piastri. New Delhi: Australia's Formula 1 driver Oscar Piastri weighed in on the revived Sandpapergate episode, which has caught Australian cricket in choppy waters following Usman Khawaja's recent revelations.Khawaja, a former Aussie cricketer, revealed in his book, Sabr, that the entire Australian team was aware of the ball-tampering plans in the infamous 2018 Cape Town Test and that they also implemented them in the previous match in Port Elizabeth.Piastri, who is himself a big cricket fan, was asked about his statement on the same ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, and he felt "it is not really a nice thing" for it to re-emerge in the headlines and hoped that it could be dealt with quickly."It has obviously been an interesting couple of weeks, that is for sure with what has been unfolding," Piastri said, as quoted by Australia's The Daily Telegraph."I know quite a few of the guys involved personally, so it is not really a nice thing to see it being brought back up necessarily, but it is what it is."Obviously I’ve got no knowledge, and I remember when it happened eight years ago, but I think for everyone, especially the Australian cricket community and Australia as a country, the quicker it can be dealt with, whatever that looks like, the better," he added.Piastri is himself a cricket fan, having previously worn Brett Lee's ODI jersey in the paddock, and he also has a picture of himself standing next to former cricketer Ricky Ponting from when he was a child.He also hosted Aussie stars Nathan Lyon, Mitchell Starc and Usman Khawaja at the McLaren Technology Centre in England ahead of the WTC 2025 final. "I know myself as a sports person that the noise around certainly is not going to be helpful, so the quicker it can be resolved and put behind us, the better for everyone," Piastri added on the saga.The Sandpaper scandal is fresh in the headlines, with differing opinions coming from all sides. Following Khawaja's claims, David Warner backed his former teammate, calling his statement "100% accurate".Current captain Pat Cummins, who was among the bowling group during that Test match, hit back at Khawaja, saying that his statement is "complete and utter nonsense".Cameron Bancroft, the on-screen implementer of the sandpaper, issued his statement in a 4000-word article in the West Australian, where he claimed that the "whole team" knew about the use of the sandpaper during the 2018 South Africa series and also that he "did not give a complete and truthful account" when he was investigated by Cricket Australia in the aftermath of the scandal. Formula 1's 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix race week is bringing significant developments both on and off the track, with Oscar Piastri facing a 10-place grid penalty, McLaren preparing technical upgrades, and Google opening a special collectibles auction for fans from November 18 to 20 in Las Vegas.According to McLaren's race preview, Piastri will start with a grid penalty after exceeding his permitted allocation of internal combustion engines. Meanwhile, discussions about Formula 1's future power units and exclusive fan experiences are adding to the attention surrounding the event.FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem indicated that the championship could eventually return to V8 engines through a social media announcement. An earlier post published by the FIA suggested that an agreement in principle had been reached with Formula 1 teams for a potential introduction in 2030, but the post was subsequently deleted.Ben Sulayem retained a separate message on his personal account, writing: "The people spoke. We listened. V8s. Coming soon," alongside an audio clip featuring the engine sound.V8 engines last appeared in Formula 1 in 2013, before the championship transitioned to 1.6-liter V6 power units. Although Ben Sulayem has previously mentioned 2030 as a possible return date, his remaining social media statement did not specify a year.McLaren confirmed that Piastri will receive a new internal combustion engine in Las Vegas following a reliability issue. Because this will be his fifth engine of the season, the Australian driver must serve a 10-place grid penalty.The team explained the decision in its race preview: "Oscar will take a new Internal Combustion Engine in Las Vegas after a reliability issue. As it is his fifth of the season, he will take a 10-place grid penalty, but he has a good chance to recover positions with overtaking in Saturday's race."McLaren also confirmed that both cars will receive an updated turbo specification enabled by the Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities system. The team expects only a relatively small performance improvement from the component.The team's statement added: "Both cars, as with the other HPP-powered cars, will be fitted with a new ADUO-enabled turbo specification: the expected performance benefit is relatively small."Further improvements are planned for the MCL40, including a revised floor. The development follows McLaren's previous upgrades in Brazil, where Lando Norris secured victory in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.Ross Hood, McLaren's Executive Director of Programme Delivery, described the latest development as an example of coordinated work across several departments.Hood said: "A new floor is arriving in Las Vegas this week, and it's a great example of our programme delivery."He also highlighted the contribution of the team's technical and manufacturing departments. Their cooperation helped McLaren maximize the results of its latest wind tunnel development work for the 40A specification.Google is also using the Las Vegas Grand Prix to introduce The Auction by Google Play, an interactive event running at The Aria Hotel from November 18 through November 20. Admission is free, while Google Play Points members receive priority access and additional benefits.Visitors can collect auction tokens by using a large interactive machine. Those tokens can be exchanged for customized keepsakes, including keychain charms and personalized 3D-printed race cars.The auction's featured collectibles include a wall-mounted replica of the 2026 McLaren Racing livery halo device and a customized Google Play collaboration jacket designed with Jeff Hamilton. Auctioneer Phyllis Kao is scheduled to lead the main auction on November 20 at 7 p.m. Pacific Time.Google Play Points members in the United States can also access exclusive digital rewards. Available items include a signed Lando Norris bucket hat, a 2026 Lando Norris 1:2 Silverstone mini helmet, and a Google Play collaboration toolbox with Toyo.Members in the Gold Plus tier can unlock a digital rewards case through the Google Play application, with opportunities to receive points boosters and physical collectibles. items.article_search_text: McLaren is hoping its 2027-focused upgrades in Las Vegas could give it an edge over Red Bull Racing — but Oscar Piastri will have to play his part. Read more at foxsports.com.au McLaren is all-in on beating Red Bull Racing to third in the teams title — but unlike last year, it doesn’t think it needs to sacrifice 2027 to do it. McLaren started the season as the defending champion. With three rounds remaining in 2026, it’s fighting to avoid a fourth-place finish — last in the frontrunning class. The team has spent almost all season in third place, its lead over the struggling Red Bull Racing peaking at a comfortable 83 points after the Italian Grand Prix. But it’s been all one-way traffic since then. McLaren was outscored by almost 17 points per weekend over the following five rounds until it was tied with Red Bull Racing on 355 points after the United States Grand Prix, where it fell to fourth place on countback. Watch the final 3 qualifying sessions in the 2026 F1® season Live and Free with Kayo Freebies. Watch FORMULA 1 HEINEKEN LAS VEGAS GRAND PRIX 2026 qualifying session on Saturday 21st November > The margin now stands at 17 points, with momentum having swung decisively towards Red Bull Racing. That Lando Norris won in Brazil only somewhat stemmed the bleeding. Max Verstappen’s monumental 20th-to-second performance underlined who holds the whip hand in this lucrative battle for minor placing. With millions of dollars on the line — never mind the pride of two teams who have shared the last four constructors titles — the next three weeks are significant ones for McLaren and Red Bull Racing. IT ALL STARTED LAST YEAR It’s no surprise that these two teams find themselves locked in a battle to avoid a last-in-class finish this season. We’ve seen this story so many times: the title-contending teams in the final season of a regulation set overcommit to the outgoing rules and find themselves undercooked for the new era. PIT TALK PODCAST: We look ahead to the beginning of the end of the Formula 1 season with this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix in one of the sport’s all-time great time zones, and it’s match point for Marc Márquez at this weekend’s MotoGP Portuguese Grand Prix. | Listen to Pit Talk below. Mercedes suffered from it in 2022. Red Bull Racing initially did too, though it rebounded quickly after having got the fundamentals right. McLaren and Ferrari will both have institutional memory of having fallen so badly off the boil in 2009 after their titanic title struggle of 2008. Now McLaren and Red Bull Racing find themselves in this familiar position. Red Bull Racing knew going into the season that it was likely to be a step behind. It was so befuddled by its downward spiral after having dominated in 2023 that it willingly committed development time to last year’s car as a troubleshooting exercise to ensure its tools were working as expected. It ended up powering Verstappen to within two points of the championship. McLaren was therefore forced to switch focus back to last year’s car to ensure one of its drivers got over the line. Though it didn’t bring any major upgrades, every day spent squeezing pace from the car was a day not dedicated to doing the same for the 2026 machine. Unsurprisingly, these two top teams found their feet in 2026 eventually, albeit too late to stop Mercedes from running away with the championship. Development trajectory, frontrunners Red Bull Racing: improving by 0.037s per race Ferrari: improving by 0.020s per race McLaren: improving by 0.012s per race Mercedes: degrading by 0.007s per race McLaren hit its straps first, in Hungary, the Netherlands and Spain, taking three poles and two wins in four races. Red Bull Racing, though, surged forward with an upgrade in Azerbaijan that got Verstappen within 0.196s of victory. He then won in Malaysia, Singapore and Mexico, and he would have been a good chance to win in Brazil had he not started from the back. McLaren, though, hasn’t kept up in that time. In what Andrea Stella described as upgrade “ping-pong”, his team has slipped backwards as others have brought upgrades — just as McLaren had done in Hungary, setting off its run of big results. Gap to fastest, last five rounds (dry) Mercedes: +0.126s Red Bull Racing: +0.266s Ferrari: +0.308s McLaren: +0.496s This would certainly suggest that third place is a done deal for Red Bull Racing. Brazil looked more like an aberration given the wet conditions and Verstappen’s strong performance regardless. But McLaren has one more bullet in the chamber. McLAREN WON’T MAKE THE SAME MISTAKE TWICE Similar to last year, the final phase of this season is being defined by which team is still upgrading its car. Mercedes’s upgrade plan has been the most novel, with just two big packages — in Canada and then in Malaysia — brought to the car. It made that choice based on its available spend within the budget cap. It had already spent big during the off-season preparing the car for launch, so it had to be wiser and more targeted about when it would commit to building parts. Red Bull Racing blew its budget early in the season because its car was in such a parlous state in the opening rounds. By the time it got to Azerbaijan in September, it admitted its 2026 development program had hit the end of the road. McLaren, though, has been more miserly, spreading out its developments throughout the year — so much so that it’s still upgrading the car now, with the end of the season on the horizon. In Brazil the team bought new front and rear wings as well as new parts to the floor. The front wing in particular was interesting as a departure from its previous philosophy. The team said it was designed with the 2027 car in mind. Notably, the drivers seemed to review that the car had become less knife-edge in the way it handled, having become increasingly peaky through the rounds prior. Now, in Las Vegas, McLaren is bringing more new parts, which McLaren boss Andrea Stella said would “form the foundation” for next year’s car. Perhaps it’s for that reason that these final rounds of 2026 have more at stake for McLaren. If these new parts are fundamental to next year’s car, underperformance will give the feeling of a lack of momentum heading into 2027. “We'll do our best to make sure it goes down to the wire and in our favour,” McLaren racing director Randy Singh told the F1 Nation podcast. “We're treating it like a mini championship on our side. “It doesn’t feel [like] any less pressure than the last couple of season finales, to be honest. We've got three races as well, which is quite nice because we've got plenty of time to try and harvest as many points as we can. “This week everyone's pretty intense with seeing what we can learn from the last race — both in the dry and in the mixed conditions — and what we can do to prepare for Vegas.” BUT IS THIS THE TRACK TO PROVE IT? The circumstances won’t be helped this weekend, however, by the circuit. Las Vegas is a true bogey track for McLaren. The car was woefully uncompetitive at the first race and then well off the boil at the second. It was in better form last year, with Norris taking pole and finishing second, but then both cars were disqualified for technical infringements. Las Vegas historical top scorers Mercedes: 86 points Red Bull Racing: 76 points Ferrari: 69 points McLaren: 18 points It’s hard to have higher expectations for McLaren this season. On paper Las Vegas is not a friendly track for the orange car. The MCL40 is at its best through high-speed corners. It’s no good down straights, where its short gears and low aero efficiency are punished. It’s also been uncompetitive all year through short, slow corners. The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is all short, slow corners and the long back straight down Las Vegas Boulevard. Some of this weekend’s upgrades are designed to boost efficiency, but it would still be a surprise to see McLaren among the leading contenders. Whether or not it can get ahead of Red Bull Racing, however, is more important than whether or not it can win. “We all see it as a challenge and a big opportunity for us to really go and get a result at a circuit that we haven't had a good result at yet,” Singh said. “We're really approaching it from that underdog sense of we've not had a good one there, but we've got a good chance to have a really good result there [this year]. “We had the car in a good window in Brazil. We need to try and make sure we do the same in Vegas. “We've got a lot of work to do to try and make sure that we hit the ground running, and that we keep optimising the package as it is now.” CAN PIASTRI MAKE THE DIFFERENCE? There’s a secondary element to this battle: the second drivers. While Verstappen and Norris have three wins apiece, Oscar Piastri and Isack Hadjar are the only frontrunners yet to take the top step of the podium. Piastri has just two podiums for the entire season, the last of which came all the way back in Miami in May. Hadjar’s third-place finish in Brazil brought him up to three for the season. Piastri is 94 points behind Norris (246–152 points, 62–38 per cent), while Hadjar — who missed three rounds through injury — is 157 points behind Verstappen (279–122 points, 70–30 per cent). In percentage terms, only rookie Arvid Lindblad, the dismissed Esteban Ocon and son-of-the-owner Lance Stroll are further adrift of their teammates by points. Piastri’s difficulties adjusting to the new regulations have been well ventilated. Hadjar’s situation is different but similarly clear, this being just his second Formula 1 season and his first at Red Bull Racing. But given Verstappen and Norris can be assumed to have got the most out of their cars, how much could a big result from either swing the battle for third? Hadjar was very strong in Las Vegas last year, qualifying eighth and finishing sixth at a strong weekend for Racing Bulls. Piastri was unspectacular. Notwithstanding that he could have qualified on the front row without some badly timed yellow flags, in the race he ended up stuck behind the superbly defensive Andrea Kimi Antonelli, locking him out of a podium finish — though he was disqualified afterwards anyway. With Red Bull Racing likely to be the stronger performer this weekend, this could be a chance for Hadjar to deliver a significant blow for his team. The next race, though, could be Piastri’s chance to hit back. Qatar, replete with high-speed bends, should be McLaren territory, and it’s by far Piastri’s strongest circuit. Piastri has never finished off the podium in Lusail, and despite never having won the race — though he would have done so easily last year were it not for McLaren’s pit stop blunder — he has a career-best average finish of 2.3. He’s never been beaten by his teammate in a race. Including sprints, he’s taking home on average 22.3 points per weekend. Assuming Formula 1 makes it to Qatar, this will be the decisive weekend to McLaren’s hopes of finishing third — and to Piastri’s contribution to that effort. Abu Dhabi is then unlikely to play to McLaren’s strengths, particularly with Max Verstappen having won five of the last six grands prix at Yas Marina. Despite being the reigning champion, McLaren is the underdog in this battle. But with an eye on 2027, it hopes it won’t be the underdog again next season. Oscar Piastri's 2026 Formula 1 struggles have shocked many, but team boss Zak Brown believes the new regulations have neutralised his competitive advantages. This season has been a difficult pill to swallow for Piastri. The Australian finds himself down in seventh, 94 points behind his team-mate Lando Norris in sixth. Whilst McLaren have also endured a difficult season thus far, Norris has enjoyed three victories and six podiums so far. Compared to Piastri's zero wins and 2 podiums in the same span. This dip in form has raised questions surrounding the 25-year-old. Some suggest he is experiencing a 'championship hangover,' following an intense battle last season. Despite leading the championship for the longest stint last season, Piastri fell short in the final rounds, finishing the season 13 points behind his team-mate in third, However, the McLaren driver explained that his form this season is due to adjusting to a new driving style. As F1 introduced new regulations, drivers across the grid found themselves learning different driving techniques required to finesse this rule set. This, according to Piastri, has led to a new 'adaptation process.' “The biggest thing has probably been the general driving style you have. Or that what you need is quite different for this year’s car compared to previous years,” Piastri explained via the F1 website. “Even in previous years, there’s been an element of adaptation and learning for that. But I think [it’s been a] combination of a few different things this year. “Obviously, the cars are smaller, the tyres are quite different. It means you really have to drive the car on the edge all of the time..." “So, it’s felt quite different to previous [cars] I’ve driven in general. That’s been quite an adaptation process. And learning to trust the car and retrain what feels like the limit is never an easy thing to try to adapt." Zak Brown highlights 2026 neutralisation as behind Oscar Piastri's dip Brown has echoed Piastri's assessment, suggesting the new regulations have changed the competitive order across the grid and taken away some of his driver's key advantages. Speaking on Sky Sports' F1 Show, the McLaren CEO pointed to the changing fortunes of several driver pairings, including Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton at Ferrari, as well as George Russell and Kimi Antonelli at Mercedes. “I think we’ve seen it mix up a little bit of the grid, right," Brown stated. “Charles [Leclerc] last year got the better of Lewis [Hamilton, at Ferrari]. Lewis is getting the better of him [now]. George [Russell] got the better of Kimi [Antonelli, last year at Mercedes]. I think it’s mixed up the grid a little bit.” The McLaren boss also identified a significant change in how Piastri's driving strengths translate to the new-generation cars. “I think if you look at Oscar’s strengths, they were kind of big, brave corners. Now all of a sudden these new big, brave corners, it’s like, hey, lift, conserve, preserve. So I think there’s a small element of him having to adapt to a new car.” Despite acknowledging Piastri's difficulties, Brown was quick to praise Norris, believing the reigning champion is currently performing at the highest level of his career. “And then, let’s not take any credit away from Lando. I’ve never seen him drive better,” the American continued. “So I think you have a combination of Lando, who’s driving the best I’ve ever seen him drive, [and] Oscar, who’s not yet clicked with it. There’s your gap. But it’s not a big gap.” READ MORE – Max Verstappen delivers hilarious Red Bull engine jibe

items.article_search_text: Oscar Piastri's woes continue with a hefty grid penalty in Las Vegas. McLaren's Oscar Piastri will exceed his internal combustion engine (ICE) allocation at the upcoming Las Vegas Grand Prix, resulting in a 10-place grid penalty for the Australian driver. Piastri will be receiving his fifth ICE of the season. Under the power-unit allocation rules, each driver can only receive four ICEs without receiving a sporting penalty. Taking a fifth, which is the first infringement, triggers a 10-place grid penalty. The positive outlook for him is that the Las Vegas Strip Circuit presents multiple overtaking opportunities. Piastri can attack on the circuit's long straights, especially if McLaren's recent upgrade packages [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/mclaren-f1-team-advances-preparations-for-2027-season] work well. PIASTRI'S RECENT STRUGGLES It has been a rough campaign this year for Piastri. From winning races and fighting for the championship in 2025, the 25-year-old has been on the back foot in terms of pace and consistency this season. He has only scored 152 points this year, which is 94 points behind his teammate, Lando Norris. Norris has also won three races and achieved six podiums in 2026. On the other hand, Piastri has not won yet, and he only has two podium finishes: a P2 in Japan and a P3 in Miami. The Miami Grand Prix was held back in the early days of May. That's how much of a struggle it has been for Piastri, especially in recent times. In the Mexican Grand Prix on November 1, the Australian driver also received a 10-second time penalty [https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/piastri-loses-p7-after-being-handed-post-race-penalty-at-mexico-city-gp.5dk3wHeak2yu7xWF0OhsRt] for causing a collision with Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad. From a P7 finish, the penalty dropped him outside the points. There's also the fact that Piastri has not advanced to the final session of qualifying in the last two races. He trails Norris in qualifying head-to-head, 13-7. BUILDING MOMENTUM IN THE LAST THREE RACES There's no way that Piastri can chase his teammate for sixth place in the Drivers' Standings. With 30 points over Red Bull's Isack Hadjar, Piastri might already be locked into seventh place. So, the Australian's focus in the three remaining races (if Qatar and Abu Dhabi push through) is to build momentum for next year. Former Haas team principal Guenther Steiner recently said [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/steiner-raises-the-alarms-piastri-does-not-have-his-seat-assured] that Piastri can't struggle like this again in 2027. If he does, McLaren boss Zak Brown might look for a replacement. He is someone quite ruthless when it comes to changing drivers" he explained on the The Red Flags podcast. The phrase summarizes the philosophy of Zak Brown, McLaren's CEO: bet on emerging talent, before it becomes a consolidated star and do it at a reasonable price. Lando Norris Backs Potential F1 Return to Argentina: “It Would Be Incredible” [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/115ee240-4551-45ac-a981-a901c9fb7cbf.jpeg] Lando Norris Backs Potential F1 Return to Argentina: “It Would Be Incredible” The Briton is excited about the possibility of Formula 1 returning to Argentine soil in the coming years. He highlights the warmth of the region's public and assures that he would love to be part of a race in the country. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/lando-norris-backs-potential-f1-return-to-argentina-it-would-be-incredible] The first name on the list is Liam Lawson. The New Zealander who has signed an exceptional 2026 season with Racing Bulls, is the driver who best embodies the profile McLaren is looking for, his adaptability, his aggressiveness on track and his consistency have made him one of the most coveted drivers on the grid. His performance in the last races with three consecutive seventh places and a memorable comeback in Mexico from the pit lane, demonstrate that he has the necessary level to compete in a top team. However his recent renewal with Racing Bulls for 2027 complicates any short-term move, even so Steiner mentions him as a future option, aware that the driver market is volatile and that opportunities can arise when least expected. The second name is Oliver Bearman: the Briton current Haas [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/haas]driver and Ferrari academy member, has demonstrated notable progress in his second full season. With 23 points an aggressive but mature driving style and a learning capacity that has impressed friends and strangers alike, Bearman represents that mix of youth and talent that Brown values so much. His link with Ferrari could be an obstacle but his contract with Haas ends in 2027 and his long-term future is far from defined, for Steiner he is an ideal candidate for a team seeking to build long-term and his youth fits perfectly with McLaren's philosophy. Ollie Bearman Opens Up: “They Were Three Horrible Weeks” [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/3240dcf9-fa2a-4264-b415-4134d33d6c2c.jpeg] Ollie Bearman Opens Up: “They Were Three Horrible Weeks” The Briton finished seventeenth in Brazil and admits that he needs to disconnect after a triple header marked by the retirements in Austin and Mexico and a slow stop in Interlagos. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/ollie-bearman-opens-up-they-were-three-horrible-weeks] Steiner's reflection also rules out other options that had been strongly rumored, when asked about the possibility of reuniting Lando Norris with Carlos Sainz, the German was blunt: he does not believe it is the most likely option: "Zak will look for someone younger" he insisted. The logic is simple: McLaren [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/mclaren]does not need a consolidated driver who charges a high salary and who has no room for growth, it needs a young talent with hunger and with potential to continue evolving and of course Lawson and Bearman fit that profile and Steiner knows it.
