items.article_search_text: The former German driver warns that if the Australian repeats a season like 2026, Zak Brown will not hesitate to look for a replacement. Oscar Piastri faces the final stretch of the season with added pressure that does not come from the track. Guenther Steiner, former Haas boss and one of the most listened-to analysts in the paddock, has launched a warning that can be interpreted as a notice to navigators: if the Australian repeats in 2027 a campaign like this year's, his future at McLaren [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/mclaren]could be in serious danger: "If he has another year like this next year, Zak will look for the next Oscar" Steiner sentenced on the The Red Flags podcast. The phrase, pronounced with the frankness that characterizes the Italian puts the focus on an uncomfortable reality for Piastri: his performance has been far below expectations. In 2025 he fought for the title until the end against his teammate Lando Norris but this year he is seventh with 152 points, light years from Max Verstappen's 279 or George Russell's 262. While Kimi Antonelli was crowned champion in Mexico, the Australian witnessed a season of ups and downs, with two podiums but without victories and with a manifest inability to adapt to the MCL40. F1 Daily: Piastri Splits From Webber, Drivers Complain to Pirelli, and Vandoorne Joins Jaguar [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/693cf553-3bd5-48e8-b6d3-fbfc3c0210e5.jpeg] F1 Daily: Piastri Splits From Webber, Drivers Complain to Pirelli, and Vandoorne Joins Jaguar Oscar Piastri has just made a major career move. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/f1-daily-piastri-splits-from-webber-drivers-complain-to-pirelli-and-vandoorne-joins-jaguar] Steiner did not stop there, when asked about the possibility of reuniting Norris with Carlos Sainz, the former driver was blunt about the strategy of Zak Brown, McLaren Racing CEO: "Zak will look for someone younger, we all know that Zak is quite good at finding young talent, Zak also likes to buy them cheap" he noted. In that context he mentioned names like that of Liam Lawson, who has just renewed with Racing Bulls or that of Oliver Bearman, Haas's great promise, Steiner's warning is not gratuitous: Brown has a reputation for being relentless when it comes to driver decisions, and Piastri [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/oscar-piastri-makes-major-career-move-what-it-means-for-his-f1-future]knows it. At 25 years old the Australian is at a crossroads, his contract with McLaren extends until 2028, but contracts in Formula 1 are as solid as the results that back them. Piastri has talent to spare as he demonstrated last year, but the irregularity of the MCL40 and his difficulty in finding the car's operating window have taken their toll. His teammate, Norris, has won three races and has scored 246 points, a difference of 94 units that reflects the gap between the two. F1 Business Weekly: Haas Adds a Bank Sponsor, F1's Billion-Dollar Revenue, and Apple's Free Las Vegas Coverage [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/9be9d8a1-933e-445d-ba38-98b724bc0e81.jpeg] F1 Business Weekly: Haas Adds a Bank Sponsor, F1's Billion-Dollar Revenue, and Apple's Free Las Vegas Coverage Haas is adding a banking giant to their list of sponsors. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/f1-business-weekly-haas-adds-a-bank-sponsor-f1s-billion-dollar-revenue-and-apples-free-las-vegas-coverage] Piastri's future will depend, to a large extent, on what happens in the three races that remain and, above all, in 2027. McLaren expects a competitive car for next season and the Australian will have to demonstrate that he can fight for victories again, if he does not, Steiner's words could become prophecy. Zak Brown is not known for his infinite patience and the driver market always has names willing to occupy a seat in a top team. Piastri is warned, the pressure does not only come from outside: his own teammate, Lando Norris, has demonstrated this year that he can carry the weight of the team and score victories even when the car is not up to the task. That constant comparison is a reminder of what McLaren expects from him, the talent is there but consistency and adaptability will mark the difference between consolidating himself as a leader or becoming a promise that never fully exploded. items.article_search_text: Oscar Piastri believes a 2026 season out of the spotlight could lead him back to the F1 promised land next year. Read more at foxsports.com.au Oscar Piastri’s fourth season has fallen short of lofty standards set by 2025, but the Australian says this year’s struggles come with a silver lining for 2027. Oscar Piastri will look back on 2026 feeling positive about his rate improvement rather than dwelling on his lack of results. Piastri, a championship contender to the final round of last year, has not kicked on in 2026, when sweeping rule changes have thrown him off his game. The Australian has been decisively behind teammate Lando Norris, the reigning champion, for most of the season, even if the margins have been relatively small. Fox Sports, available on Kayo Sports, is the only place to watch every practice, qualifying session and race in the 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship™ LIVE in 4K | Get Kayo now > McLaren’s relative lack of competitiveness for much of the year has been an additional difficulty, though Piastri has been a step behind Norris at the few rounds at which the car has been a genuine victory threat. But McLaren has seen signs of progress from the Australian as the year has progressed, and in Singapore last month CEO Zak Brown said Piastri was fundamentally back to where he was in 2025 in terms of his confidence with the car despite few headline results to show for it. As just one example, despite finishing sixth in Brazil behind the victorious Norris, Piastri’s race pace was respectable for much of the grand prix. Though he admitted 2026 has “definitely been tough”, Piastri told the F1 website that he was finding joy in “trying to make progress”. “I've always tried to remove results from what success looks like,” he said. “Of course results do help, but especially when you're not in a position to win races — whether it be because of the car or the kind of struggles I've had this year — sometimes a win and a successful weekend looks like improvement rather than perfection. “That's brought me joy for sure. There's been some very strong weekends this year that I've been really happy with. [I’m] just trying to work through those things.” The contrast between Piastri and Norris this season has been stark, particularly at the weekends when more has been up for grabs, with the Englishman rarely dropping an opportunity this year. However, it’s been clear from early on that there would be little on the line for McLaren and its drivers this year. Mercedes’s strong start all but guaranteed both titles, even if the field has closed during the year. The team is fourth in the standings and chasing Red Bull Racing for third, while Norris and Piastri are unlikely to finish higher or lower than sixth and seventh respectively in the drivers championship. The team’s step down under new regulations has been a blessing in disguise for Piastri, who has had a chance to do his learning without the pressure of needing to contend for a title in the hope that he’ll be ready for a championship challenge next year if circumstances allow. The same applies to some of the weaknesses that undermined his 2025 campaign later in the year. “Even some of the challenges from last year, they weren't completely dissimilar to what I've got this year, and I feel like I've definitely made a lot of progress on that in general,” he said. “These last few races are definitely going to be another challenge in terms of testing where I'm at, in terms of developing those skills. “Having that challenge has been tough, obviously, but getting through it and then continuing to work on it [is] ultimately going to be rewarding and [will] hopefully set me up for whatever car we get [in future]. “Definitely between myself and the pretty close and intimate engineering team around me, we've learned a lot about each other and how we get the most out of ourselves [as well as] how we get more out of ourselves. "That's been a good process to go through for sure.” Oscar Piastri vs Lando Norris, 2026 so far Qualifying head to head: Norris leads 13-7 Qualifying differential: Norris ahead 1.7 places Time differential: Norris faster by 0.111s (dry only) Race head to head: Norris leads 10-4 Race differential: Norris ahead 1.9 places Race pace differential: Norris faster by 0.3s Points: Norris leads 246-152 (62–38 per cent) Some of the changes to the cars this season have played into Piastri’s weaknesses. The cars are generally lower in grip given the reduced aerodynamic load, and the Australian is at his best when he can exploit high-grip conditions. Further, though, is the way the 2026 car wants to be hustled. Whereas in previous seasons Piastri has been able to achieve a car’s peak performance by driving fractionally below the limit, this year’s car prefers to be pushed to or beyond the limit at all times to deliver its best. Piastri isn’t as comfortable reacting to a peaky car — and the problem has been exacerbated by McLaren’s 2026 challenger being particularly unpredictable at the limit, as even Norris has complained. “You really have to drive the car on the edge all of the time — certainly our car, I don't know what others think of it,” he said. “You're always driving on the edge to an extent, but this year it's really always taking you beyond the edge of trying to salvage things. It's felt quite different to previous [cars] and even a lot of the previous cars I've driven in general. “That's been quite an adaptation process, and learning to trust the car and retrain what feels like the limit is never an easy thing to try and adapt. “It's been tougher than I expected with trying to get to grips with the car … it's definitely thrown in a lot of challenges, and I feel like I've had to change a lot of things in how I drive or certainly tweak things. “But I feel I'm making some progress now in the second half of this year, so [I’m] just trying to continue that.” MORE FORMULA 1 'DID IT FOR AUSTRALIA': How Ricciardo’s ‘bogan’ act came to define his F1 wins... and the ‘loose’ history that inspired it SILLY SEASON: Final piece left in F1's 2027 driver puzzle as Red Bull finally makes contract call 'NOT THE REALITY': Alarming truth about F1's 'new dynasty' claims... and what it means for 2027 Though third in the constructors championship will be of limited consolation to the team that won the last two titles — notwithstanding the boost in prize money — the final three weekends of the season are critical to Piastri and McLaren preparing for a 2027 both hope will bring far bigger prizes. “Everyone is still very determined to get back to where we know we can be,’ Piastri said. “I think we're on our way back there; development and upgrades have always been a strong point for us, and hopefully we can just keep pushing. “The teams around us have definitely raised the bar, but I know that we can raise it even higher.” Oscar Piastri splits from F1 legend manager Mark Webber Motorsport: Liam Lawson will remain with Racing Bulls for the 2027 Formula 1 season alongside teammate Arvid Lindblad after the team confirms its unchanged driver line-up.
